page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.2xlarge is an instance in the Big data family, configured with 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores using an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The server runs on a KVM hypervisor with dedicated CPU allocation, providing 32 GB of system RAM (4.0 GB per core) and an L3 cache of 33 MB. It includes hardware flag support for AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, and FMA. Networking features a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and the system contains no dedicated GPUs.

Storage configuration is the primary differentiator of this server type, bundling 23,622 GB of local HDD storage. Compute and memory benchmark results reflect an older hardware generation. Geekbench reports a single-core score of 957.0 and a multi-core score of 3546.0, while stress-ng multi-core yields 5,838.18, both falling in the bottom 25% tier. PassMark overall CPU performance registers at 7,009.91, placing it in the middle 50% tier. Memory benchmarks show uncached write bandwidth of 34.88 GB/sec in the middle 50% tier, but read bandwidth and general operations score in the lower percentiles, such as PassMark database operations at 2,165.2 and Redis SET throughput at 5.63 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.d1.2xlarge prioritizes extreme local disk capacity per compute unit over raw CPU speed. Because performance scores in compression, software compilation, and in-memory caches land in lower percentile tiers, workloads requiring fast random I/O or dense compute throughput represent suboptimal fits. The instance is suited for high-density sequential storage architectures, such as Hadoop HDFS nodes, big data batch analytics, log aggregation pipelines, and offline data archiving.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.2xlarge is a big data-focused instance providing 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores on a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor, paired with 32 GB of system RAM. Its defining technical attribute is a bundled 23,622 GB local HDD array alongside a 3 Gbps network baseline. The architecture lacks integrated GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 3546.0 and stress-ng multi-core score of 5838.18, place CPU and memory throughput predominantly in the lower quartile, though PassMark CPU overall reaches the middle 50% bracket. The hardware tradeoffs emphasize massive sequential local storage density rather than intensive single-thread performance or fast random I/O. As such, the ecs.d1.2xlarge is primarily suited for distributed storage platforms, Hadoop data nodes, batch ETL operations, and large-scale log archiving.
